scenes.visual: Title card: Followers, Glue and the Reader.

scenes.tts: A growth cone meets many bundles of axons. Its filopodia touch several. Why does it join just one?
scenes.visual: A growth cone arrives among many parallel axon bundles; its filopodia reach several. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: A growth cone meets many bundles of axons. Its filopodia touch several. Why does it join just one?

scenes.tts: When axons grow bundled together, they are fasciculated. When one leaves its bundle, it defasciculates.
scenes.visual: Axons bundled together, labelled fasciculated. One axon peels away, labelled defasciculates.
scenes.narration: When axons grow bundled together, they are fasciculated. When one leaves its bundle, it defasciculates.

scenes.tts: In grasshopper embryos, Raper, Bastiani and Goodman followed a neuron called G.
scenes.visual: A schematic grasshopper central nervous system with many longitudinal bundles. One neuron is labelled G.
scenes.narration: In grasshopper embryos, Raper, Bastiani and Goodman followed a neuron called G.

scenes.tts: Its growth cone joins one bundle, the A P fascicle, made of axons from neurons called A and P. It grows along the P axons.
scenes.caption: Its growth cone joins one bundle, the A/P fascicle, made of axons from neurons called A and P. It grows along the P axons.
scenes.visual: G joins one bundle labelled A/P fascicle, whose axons are labelled A and P, and rides along the P axons.
scenes.narration: Its growth cone joins one bundle, the A/P fascicle, made of axons from neurons called A and P. It grows along the P axons.

scenes.tts: Before G arrived, the team killed the P neurons, the A neurons, or both.
scenes.visual: Two panels. Left: P axons removed. Right: A axons removed. G not yet arrived in either.
scenes.narration: Before G arrived, the team killed the P neurons, the A neurons, or both.

scenes.tts: If any bundle would do, G should take a neighbour. What did G do?
scenes.visual: On-screen text: What did G do? Neighbouring bundles sit within reach of the filopodia.
scenes.narration: If any bundle would do, G should take a neighbour. What did G do?

scenes.visual: Hold on the two panels. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: Without the P axons, G failed to extend far along its route. It wandered, branched abnormally, and took no other bundle.
scenes.visual: Left panel: G extends only a short way along its normal route, then wanders and branches abnormally; it does not follow any of the neighbouring bundles.
scenes.narration: Without the P axons, G failed to extend far along its route. It wandered, branched abnormally, and took no other bundle.

scenes.tts: Without only the A axons, G behaved normally.
scenes.visual: Right panel: G joins what is left of the fascicle and grows forward normally.
scenes.narration: Without only the A axons, G behaved normally.

scenes.visual: A table builds on screen: none killed, normal; A killed, normal; P killed, normal route fails; A and P killed, normal route fails.

scenes.tts: G needs something particular to the P axons. Hence the labeled pathway hypothesis: bundles carry surface labels that growth cones recognize.
scenes.visual: On-screen text: labeled pathway hypothesis. Bundles carry small coloured tags; the G growth cone carries a matching receptor for one colour.
scenes.narration: G needs something particular to the P axons. Hence the labeled pathway hypothesis: bundles carry surface labels that growth cones recognize.

scenes.tts: In the fruit fly, the search found adhesion molecules, not a unique label for each bundle.
scenes.visual: A Drosophila embryo with its motor nerves stained (labelled AI illustration).
scenes.narration: In the fruit fly, the search found adhesion molecules, not a unique label for each bundle.

scenes.tts: Fasciclin two can bind Fasciclin two on a neighbouring axon. Without it, axons that travel together in certain pathways drift apart.
scenes.caption: Fasciclin II can bind Fasciclin II on a neighbouring axon. Without it, axons that travel together in certain pathways drift apart.
scenes.visual: Two axons held by paired Fasciclin II molecules. Remove them, and the axons drift apart.
scenes.narration: Fasciclin II can bind Fasciclin II on a neighbouring axon. Without it, axons that travel together in certain pathways drift apart.

scenes.tts: In a separate experiment, extra Fasciclin two kept motor axons stuck in their nerve. They bypassed their muscles.
scenes.caption: In a separate experiment, extra Fasciclin II kept motor axons stuck in their nerve. They bypassed their muscles.
scenes.visual: A motor axon with extra Fasciclin II stays in the nerve and runs past its muscle.
scenes.narration: In a separate experiment, extra Fasciclin II kept motor axons stuck in their nerve. They bypassed their muscles.

scenes.tts: Opposite changes, opposite results. The amount of adhesion between axons matters.
scenes.visual: A dial labelled adhesion: low, axons drift apart; high, axons stay stuck. Small print: a qualitative comparison of two experiments.
scenes.narration: Opposite changes, opposite results. The amount of adhesion between axons matters.

scenes.tts: A second gene, beaten path, makes a protein on motor axons. Without it, motor axons fail to leave their nerve.
scenes.visual: Three-panel strip, first two panels: a normal axon exits toward its muscle; a beaten path mutant axon stays in the nerve.
scenes.narration: A second gene, beaten path, makes a protein on motor axons. Without it, motor axons fail to leave their nerve.

scenes.tts: Now reduce Fasciclin two in a beaten path mutant. What happens at the choice point?
scenes.caption: Now reduce Fasciclin II in a beaten path mutant. What happens at the choice point?
scenes.visual: Third panel is blank, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Now reduce Fasciclin II in a beaten path mutant. What happens at the choice point?

scenes.visual: Hold on the strip with the blank third panel. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: The bypass defect is suppressed. Motor axons can often leave their nerve again.
scenes.visual: Third panel fills in: an example axon exits again. Label: suppression, not complete rescue.
scenes.narration: The bypass defect is suppressed. Motor axons can often leave their nerve again.

scenes.tts: Lowering adhesion makes up for losing Beat. So Beat works at least partly against adhesion between axons.
scenes.visual: A balance: axon-to-axon adhesion on one side, the pull to leave the nerve on the other. Lowering adhesion tips it toward exit. Beat is not drawn touching the Fasciclin II links. Small print: genetic suppression, not a test of direct binding.
scenes.narration: Lowering adhesion makes up for losing Beat. So Beat works at least partly against adhesion between axons.

scenes.tts: Beat also helps motor axons recognize a pathway cue called Sidestep.
scenes.visual: A motor axon leaves the nerve toward tissue labelled Sidestep; Beat on its surface is highlighted.
scenes.narration: Beat also helps motor axons recognize a pathway cue called Sidestep.

scenes.tts: Last, the same cue can mean different things. In a simple comparison, netrin one can attract growth cones carrying the receptor D C C.
scenes.caption: Last, the same cue can mean different things. In a simple comparison, netrin-1 can attract growth cones carrying the receptor DCC.
scenes.visual: A netrin gradient. A growth cone with DCC turns toward the cue-rich side. Label: one example, under stated conditions.
scenes.narration: Last, the same cue can mean different things. In a simple comparison, netrin-1 can attract growth cones carrying the receptor DCC.

scenes.tts: With a second receptor, U N C five, beside D C C, it can repel them instead.
scenes.caption: With a second receptor, UNC5, beside DCC, it can repel them instead.
scenes.visual: A second growth cone with DCC and UNC5 turns away from the same gradient. Label: one example, under stated conditions.
scenes.narration: With a second receptor, UNC5, beside DCC, it can repel them instead.

scenes.tts: The growth cone's internal state, and the surface beneath it, can also flip the response.
scenes.visual: One growth cone with DCC; a dial labelled internal state and a strip of substrate beneath it; its turn flips from toward to away.
scenes.narration: The growth cone's internal state, and the surface beneath it, can also flip the response.

scenes.tts: A cue is a message. The receptors and internal state of the growth cone decide what it means.
scenes.visual: The same netrin cloud, two growth cones turning opposite ways. On-screen text: the reader decides.
scenes.narration: A cue is a message. The receptors and internal state of the growth cone decide what it means.

scenes.tts: So followers choose which axons to ride. And the reader decides what a cue means.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: followers choose their bundle; the reader decides what a cue means.
scenes.narration: So followers choose which axons to ride. And the reader decides what a cue means.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
